description: The wire format of the service's deployment-local bootstrap and recovery transport (service/src/local_transport, module docs "Protocol", "Operations" and "Errors"): the request members of each op, the reply shapes, the closed set of refusal codes, the framing and the size limits, with golden request and reply lines. Inferred: no contract text fixes this wire format (the service's module docs say so); the service's code is the source, and status stays "proposed" until a contract states it. Framing: one request per connection; the client writes one JSON object on one line, the newline, then closes its write half (shutdown(SHUT_WR)); no byte may follow the newline; the server answers one JSON object on one line with its newline and closes. Requests: op first, then the op's members in the order listed under ops, no whitespace, byte values in lowercase hexadecimal, strings escaped as serde_json escapes them. Replies: serde_json's compact output, each success with exactly its members in the order listed under replies, every refusal {"error":"<code>"} and nothing else. framing.max_request_bytes is the service's MAX_REQUEST_BYTES; framing.max_reply_bytes is the client's own cap, 4 MiB, a defence against a misbehaving peer: the service bounds every reply, since a revoked_credential_ids list holds at most framing.max_revoked_ids_per_reply IDs (the service's page size; the restore reply lists the first of them in byte order, status the next page after revoked_after); a reply over it is an unknown outcome (reconcile first). A member type written <type>|null (status only) is a member that is always present, its value of that type or null. default_limits are the service's default time limits (Settings::default(): deadline, transaction_timeout and idle_timeout, in whole seconds) and the client's default total wait, their sum: the longest an accepted connection lasts on a default server, from the accept (the server's settings are tunable and not discoverable by the client); operator/tests/local_exchange and tests/harness/local_transport_wire.rs read them. The golden lines of exchange are the bytes the real service sent, with the given ID seed (SequentialIds) and clock, for a fresh database: the preview and restore signature is over the issued challenge M by the bootstrap recovery key (a test key). To regenerate exchange and the golden lines it names (the requests and replies of bootstrap, issue_challenge, preview, restore and status, and the not_restorable and conflict replies; every ID in them is a SequentialIds ID of exchange.id_seed): add for the time a test to tests/harness (wired in tests/pg.rs, run once with the database environment tests/pg.rs documents, then removed) that serves the service's LocalTransport::new(pool, a clock fixed at exchange.now_micros, SequentialIds::with_seed(exchange.id_seed), None), default Settings, on a fresh database (skyoauth-scenarios' TestDb, migrated), sends the requests of exchange.steps in order, each on its own connection framed as above, and prints each reply line verbatim. The requests are built from test keys: the bootstrap recovery key is the Ed25519 public key of the seed of 32 bytes 0x51 (SEED in service/tests/local_transport.rs), the new recovery key that of 32 bytes 0x52 (NEW_SEED); credential_spki is the Ed25519 SubjectPublicKeyInfo prefix 302a300506032b6570032100 followed by 32 bytes 0x01 (bootstrap) or 0x02 (issue_challenge); trust_anchor_ref is deployment/operator-ca and instance_id the bootstrap line's; the preview and restore signature is the 0x51 key's Ed25519 signature over the bytes of the challenge the issue_challenge reply carries. Ed25519 signatures are deterministic, so the same inputs give the same lines; a change to the ID format, to the order in which the transport draws IDs, to M or to a reply shape changes them, and tests/harness/local_transport_wire.rs (the_golden_exchange_is_the_services) fails until they are regenerated. The status requests ask nothing (before the bootstrap), the bootstrap's credential_spki (after it: the instance, recovery key and mTLS key enrolled; enrolled_trust_anchor_sha256 is the lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 of the UTF-8 bytes of the trust_anchor_ref the bootstrap sent), and the issued operation ID (after the restore: restored, its replacement's IDs and the revoked count and page), then with revoked_after its last revoked ID (an empty page); status draws no ID. issue_challenge_escapes and unknown_replies are written by hand, not captured. unknown_replies are bytes the operator's client must classify as an unknown outcome (reconcile first), with the reason it gives. Checked by operator/tests/local_wire (skyoauth-operator, every member) and tests/harness/local_transport_wire.rs (skyoauth-scenarios, against the service: constants, codes, golden requests through the real transport with an unreachable store, and the exchange on a database). Edited in place on 2026-11-27 (lead ruling Q6, docs/proposals/local-read-operation.md; no deployed peer exists, so the version stays 1): the status op and its reply shape, the <type>|null notation, framing.max_revoked_ids_per_reply, the restored reply's revoked_credential_count and capped list, the status golden lines and exchange steps, and the unknown_replies of the parser's list checks (a list longer than the page size, unsorted or repeated, in a restored and in a status reply) and of the status shape (a missing member, a value where null belongs, an unknown state).

applies_when: the peer's UID is neither the service UID nor root (0), or its credentials cannot be read; answered before the request is read

a malformed or oversized request: over 64 KiB with its newline, a byte after the newline, the end of the stream before it, invalid UTF-8 or JSON, a root that is not an object, an unknown op, a missing, repeated, unknown or mistyped member

a value the transport's checks refuse: not lowercase hexadecimal, an instance_id that is not a lowercase UUIDv7, a key that is not a canonical Ed25519 point of large order, a DER that is not one SubjectPublicKeyInfo, a bad trust_anchor_ref, an operation ID with a NUL
bootstrap is closed or the instance ID is not the stored one
no challenge can be issued (no closed recovery state), or the replacement key is already registered
the registry's NotFound, StaleRevision, AlreadyExists, Guard and foreign-key class invariants
the signed response does not authorize a restoration, for every reason (a bad signature, an expired, consumed or unknown challenge, an unchanged recovery key): one code, no reason

the store was unavailable or the transaction was aborted (serialization failure, deadlock, lock or statement timeout, a lost connection, a failed BEGIN or COMMIT of those); nothing was written, unless a failed COMMIT was answered this way: its outcome is then unknown (a bootstrap, issue_challenge or restore is reconciled first, never repeated at once; a preview writes nothing)

a server or data-integrity error, an ID generator failure, an unreadable timestamp; nothing was written, unless a failed COMMIT was answered this way: its outcome is then unknown (a bootstrap, issue_challenge or restore is reconciled first, never repeated at once; a preview writes nothing)
